buyer_account_undeclared_note: No buy can be proposed until a funded buyer account is declared: propose refuses without --buyer-account and refuses one that fails checksum. An empty feed says so rather than being absent.
check_without_us: block_info on a node you chose, for any block hash below

how_to_be_paid.we_need: your published price, in your words, and an address that passes checksum.
how_to_be_paid.what: Publish a price for an output. We send the full amount before you deliver.
how_to_be_paid.you_need: an address to be paid at. No account with us, no clone, no code of ours.

notes: Every buy here was paid BEFORE the work arrived. The send block is the first move and it is ours.
not_delivered_count is published, not withheld. A buyer that only publishes its wins is not evidence of anything.

Nothing here judges whether what arrived was any good. `delivered` means bytes with a matching digest; the buyer's verdict on usefulness is acceptance_receipt.py's, and conflating the two is the defect six agents named.

Every digest here is published as two 32-character halves: join them for the digest. They are split because this repository's secret gate refuses any standalone run of 64 hex characters in a committed file - a Nano seed looks exactly like one - and weakening that gate so a feed can print a digest would be the wrong trade.

recipes.amount_to_send_raw: order_bound_amount.derive(order_digest, price_raw)['pay_raw'] - the price plus a tag in 1..999999 derived from the order digest, so a stranger recomputes which order a block paid for without asking us.
recipes.order_digest: blake2b-256 over bytes.fromhex(scope_digest) concatenated with order_key.encode('utf-8'). The scope digest enters as its 32 RAW bytes, never as the 64 characters of hex text, which is the byte rule order_bound_amount.tag_for keeps.

sellers_paid_note: sellers_paid and distinct_sellers_paid are one number under the two names a reader looks for: distinct payee accounts, decoded to public keys, whose buy reached paid or later.
